findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancellation aborts the whole cancellation loop permanently
findings.body: The `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop is wrapped in a single outer `try`/`catch`. If the `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends` request throws for one reminder (invalid/expired batch id, already-cancelled batch, transient 4xx/5xx), the catch is hit, the loop aborts, and none of the remaining reminders in the batch are cancelled; the `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` promises collected so far are never awaited either (Prisma promises are lazy), so nothing is removed from the DB. Because the next cron run re-selects the same rows ordered the same way, a single permanently-failing reminder blocks every other cancellation forever and reminder emails for cancelled/rescheduled bookings keep going out — exactly the bug this PR is meant to fix. The try/catch (and the delete) should be inside the loop, per reminder.

findings.title: immediateDelete path re-introduces the SendGrid pending-cancellation limit and leaks DB rows
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` issues the SendGrid `status: "cancel"` request straight away and returns early, without deleting or flagging the `workflowReminder` row. Two consequences: (1) every reschedule (`handleNewBooking.ts`, which passes `true`) and every workflow/step deletion still consumes one of SendGrid's max-100 pending cancellation slots — the root cause described in the PR body — so the limit can still be exhausted and subsequent cancellations silently fail; (2) for the reschedule path (where the old booking row is not deleted and therefore nothing cascades) the stale reminder row survives with `scheduled: true` and a `referenceId`, and `cancelled` left null, so it is only cleaned up when the scheduledDate finally passes. Either route the reschedule case through the deferred `cancelled` flag like cancellation, or delete the row when cancelling immediately.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget; the `cancelled` flag may never be persisted
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but are invoked inside `forEach` without `await`, and their results are no longer collected into `prismaPromises` (as the previous `remindersToDelete` array was). The handler can therefore return its HTTP response before the `workflowReminder.update({ cancelled: true })` / `delete` queries have executed. On a serverless runtime the function can be frozen/terminated right after the response, so the flag is never written and the cron job will never cancel the scheduled SendGrid email — the reminder for a cancelled booking is still delivered. The same unawaited pattern was introduced in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (requestReschedule) and `handleNewBooking.ts`. These calls should be awaited (e.g. `await Promise.all(...)`).

findings.title: Deferred cancellation can miss SendGrid's cancellation deadline for near-term reminders
findings.body: Cancellation is deferred to a cron that runs every ~15 minutes and only picks up reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. A booking cancelled shortly before its reminder's send time (e.g. 12 minutes before) will only have the SendGrid cancel request issued on the next cron tick, which can be less than SendGrid's required 10-minute lead time before `sendAt` — in that case the cancel is rejected/ignored and the reminder email is still sent. Worse, the `deleteMany` at line 34 removes EMAIL reminders whose `scheduledDate` is already in the past before the cancellation block runs, so such rows are dropped without any cancellation attempt and without any log. Consider cancelling immediately when `scheduledDate` is near (while keeping the deferred path for far-future reminders) so the pending-cancellation quota is still protected.

findings.title: Unused `Prisma` import left behind after removing BatchPayload usage
findings.body: The import block was changed from `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` to a value import that still includes `Prisma`, but all `Prisma.BatchPayload` usages were removed in this diff, so `Prisma` is now unused in this file. With the repo's no-unused-vars/consistent-type-imports lint rules this fails CI; the formatting of the new import block (no trailing comma on the last specifier) will also be flagged by the prettier check.

findings.title: Cancellation query does not restrict to EMAIL reminders with a reference id
findings.body: `remindersToCancel` selects every `workflowReminder` with `cancelled: true`, without filtering on `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`, `scheduled: true` or `referenceId: { not: null }`. Today only email reminders are ever flagged, but any future/manual row with another method (or a null `referenceId`) would be POSTed to SendGrid as a `batch_id`, producing an error that — given the shared try/catch — aborts the whole cancellation loop. Add the explicit filters so this endpoint only ever handles rows it can act on.

findings.title: No automated coverage for the cancelled-reminder flow
findings.body: This is the second attempt at fixing reminders being sent for cancelled/rescheduled bookings (the previous fix in #6991 silently stopped working in production). The PR adds a new `cancelled` field plus a new cron branch but no test asserting that cancelling or rescheduling a booking marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, that the cron issues the SendGrid cancel and removes the row, and that a failing cancellation does not block the others. Without a test the regression can recur unnoticed, as it already did.
